posts.text:
Majo Aguilar y MXKA cantarán los himnos en el NFL Mexico City Game 2026

Majo Aguilar y MXKA interpretarán los himnos de México y Estados Unidos antes del juego entre Minnesota Vikings y San Francisco 49ers en el Estadio Banorte.Por Brenda Aguilar | Reportera                                      Majo Aguilar y MXKA interpretarán los himnos nacionales de México y Estados Unidos, respectivamente, antes del partido entre los Minnesota Vikings y los San Francisco 49ers, correspondiente al Mexico City Game 2026 de la National Football League (NFL). El encuentro se disputará el domingo 22 de noviembre a las 19:20 horas, tiempo del centro de México, en el Estadio Banorte.La participación de ambas artistas formará parte de la ceremonia previa al encuentro, que marcará el regreso de la NFL a la Ciudad de México con un partido de temporada regular. El duelo corresponde a la Semana 11 de la temporada 2026 y será transmitido en horario estelar.El partido también contará con la presentación de The Warning durante el medio tiempo. El trío originario de Monterrey fue anunciado previamente como responsable del espectáculo musical, presentado por American Express, en el Estadio Banorte.Majo Aguilar interpretará el Himno NacionalMajo Aguilar, cantante y compositora de música mexicana, será la encargada de interpretar el Himno Nacional Mexicano antes del inicio del encuentro.La artista ha desarrollado una propuesta que combina elementos del mariachi y la música ranchera con influencias contemporáneas. De acuerdo con su sello discográfico, Universal Music México, su repertorio acumula más de 535 millones de reproducciones globales.La cantante señaló que representar a México en el partido representa un motivo de orgullo y agradeció a la NFL por la invitación para participar en la ceremonia.Su presencia en el Mexico City Game se suma a otras presentaciones realizadas en escenarios mexicanos y acontecimientos deportivos de relevancia, mientras mantiene una carrera vinculada con la nueva generación de intérpretes de música mexicana.MXKA llevará su propuesta bilingüeMXKA, cantautora nacida en Oakland, California, interpretará el Himno Nacional de Estados Unidos. Su propuesta musical combina elementos de la música mexicana con R&B contemporáneo y letras bilingües.La artista ha descrito su estilo como R&B Tumbados y ha construido su propuesta a partir de sus raíces familiares mexicanas y estadounidenses. Su madre es originaria de la Ciudad de México y su padre es de Luisiana.MXKA señaló que cantar el himno estadounidense en la Ciudad de México representa una conexión con distintas partes de su historia personal y artística, además de permitirle llevar sus raíces mexicanas y negras a un escenario internacional.La cantante también ha participado en actividades relacionadas con grandes eventos deportivos. Su trabajo ha sido difundido por medios como Billboard, KQED y Remezcla, mientras su sencillo “La Vuelta” impulsó un crecimiento significativo de sus oyentes en Spotify.NFL regresa a Ciudad de MéxicoEl partido entre los Vikings y los 49ers será el regreso de la NFL a México después del encuentro disputado en 2022 entre San Francisco y los Arizona Cardinals en el entonces Estadio Azteca.La NFL anunció un acuerdo para disputar partidos de temporada regular en la Ciudad de México durante tres años a partir de 2026, con el Estadio Banorte como sede.El duelo de noviembre será además el primer Sunday Night Football de temporada regular que la liga programe fuera de Estados Unidos. El calendario oficial establece que Vikings y 49ers se enfrentarán a las 20:20 horas del Este, equivalente a las 19:20 horas en México.La temporada internacional de 2026 contempla nueve partidos fuera de Estados Unidos, distribuidos en cuatro continentes y siete países, una cifra récord para la NFL. México forma parte nuevamente de ese calendario con el encuentro de la Semana 11. –sn–Masoud Pezeshkian | ONU – Loey Felipe¡Conéctate con Sociedad Noticias! posts.text: Cam Heyward details how the offense can improve: “We can have more communication. We can have better execution. You gotta take what defenses give you. posts.text: Mike McCarthy on moving forward with the offense: “Specific to last week, we had protection challenges. The week before, we were able to get the shots off and just didn't get them executed. After two weeks, just like anything, you start Monday and you want to marry the run to the pass and the [play]-action game. Hopefully, you get those opportunities called, get them off and get the results you're looking for. Also, the ability to run the ball, and in particular, run-pass options. Aaron does a really good job with that. You don't ever want to be doing things one way. It's important to stretch all the quadrants of the field. You want to attack them underneath, attack them in the intermediate, get your downfield throws, and get your 'shot plays' off the call sheet.” #Steelers #NFL

posts.text: The Commanders have officially ruled out QB Jayden Daniels with a left elbow injury.

posts.author: NFL.com
posts.text: Bears QB Caleb Williams suffers hamstring injury in loss to Vikings - NFL.com

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text: Ladd McConkey is officially active.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: Welcome back, TreVeyon Henderson.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: The Packers have ruled out WR Jayden Reed (neck) and RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee).

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to go on Sunday after being limited some this week, sources say. Coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters this week it was minor.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: Ravens pass-rusher Trey Hendrickson, who broke a finger into several pieces this week, is slated to play on Sunday with cast on his hand, sources say.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: Chiefs star DT Chris Jones, who has dealt with a calf injury, should be good to go for tonight’s game, sources say.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text:
Chargers WR Ladd McConkey, dealing with a cracked rib, practiced Friday and has improved more steadily than anticipated. The team did not elevate a WR and he’s pushing to play, sources say.

There is optimism that he can go today, barring a setback.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: The Falcons are getting healthy, with G Chris Lindstrom (concussion) clearing the protocol and CB AJ Terrell (shoulder) also expected to play, sources say.

posts.text: NFL Week 2 injury report: Puka Nacua, Joe Burrow questionable, Zay Flowers, Michael Pittman, Kyler Murray out - CBS Sports

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text:
Injury news:
— Patriots CB Carlton Davis III has been downgraded to out vs the Steelers.
— Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) won’t practice today and will be questionable for MNF.
— Packers DT Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion) downgraded to out, but edge Lukas Van Ness has cleared concussion protocol.

posts.author: rapsheet.bsky.social
posts.text: Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. is going to be placed on Injured Reserve, sources say, giving him four weeks to recover from his ankle sprain. He’ll be designated to return and should be back shortly.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Deshaun Watson and Baker Mayfield meet on Sunday in Tampa for the first time since one of the biggest trades, and wildest weeks, in NFL history. 

An in-depth look at how it happened, and the fallout for all involved, in my latest dispatch at The Sweep:

tompelissero.substack.com/p/week-2-ins...

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr. is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in today’s win over Tennessee, sources say. 

X-rays were negative. Cooper, the first-round pick, will have an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text: Myles Garrett is now set to miss games against the Giants, Broncos, Eagles and Bills. L.A. hosts the Cardinals in Week 6.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Rams star Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery on his ailing knee and is headed to injured reserve, sources tell The Ringer and Netflix Sports.

Garrett has been dealing with lower-leg pain and wasn’t himself in Thursday’s opener. The hope is he’s back in four weeks.

posts.author: CBS Sports
posts.text: NFL Week 1 injuries: Giants' Malik Nabers, Bears' Rome Odunze listed as questionable - CBS Sports

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the team got good news on Sam Darnold, who underwent tests that ruled out a hip fracture. Still more tests to come. But Macdonald sounded upbeat about the initial prognosis.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Baker Mayfield’s new contract with the Bucs got him to the $55 million benchmark he wanted. It also prevented a scenario where Tampa Bay would have to carry a nonnegotiable cap number of nearly $80 million for its QB next season.

More in The Sweep: tompelissero.substack.com/p/week-1-not...

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Drake Maye wasn’t the only QB hurting in the Super Bowl. Sam Darnold spent most of the playoffs in a rehab progression for an external oblique strain as the Seahawks made a championship run.

More ahead of tonight’s rematch in a free column at The Sweep: tompelissero.substack.com/p/week-1-not...

posts.text: Sources: The #Seahawks are signing veteran QB Drew Lock, bringing him back to Seattle for a second stint. He will backup Sam Darnold.

posts.author: schultzreport.bsky.social
posts.text:
Sources: Colorado QB Shedeur Sanders is scheduled to visit the #Raiders early next week. 

Las Vegas holds the No. 6 pick in the draft. They have been doing work on QBs and have other QB prospects also coming into their building.

posts.author: schultzreport.bsky.social
posts.text: Spoke with an NFL assistant GM about Alabama QB Jalen Milroe: “He’s one of the most intriguing guys in the entire draft. There’s a narrative that he’s just a running quarterback, but that’s way off...

posts.author: schultzreport.bsky.social
posts.text:
Former #Bucs OC Byron Leftwich is back in coaching as he is joining Deion Sanders’ staff at Colorado.

Leftwich interviewed for multiple NFL jobs this past cycle (Pats HC, Seahawks OC) but now makes the move to college.

posts.author: kimberleymartin.bsky.social
posts.text: #Bears GM Ryan Poles, via team statement: “This morning, after meeting with George and Kevin, we informed Matt of our decision to move in a different direction with the leadership of our football team and the head coaching position…”

posts.author: kimberleymartin.bsky.social
posts.text:
Matt Eberflus at 9:30a: “I’m confident I’ll be prepping for SF and coaching this team.”

Matt Eberflus at noon: FIRED.

(Why would the #Bears let that man address reporters, knowing he wouldn’t make it thru the week, let alone the day?)

posts.author: kimberleymartin.bsky.social
posts.text: Will this game be over before I have to leave for Cincinnati on Saturday 🫠
